question.problem:
Given that the minor of ${m}_{21}$ is $11$, find all the possible values of $y$ in the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}y & \frac{3}{2} & y \\ 25 & 4-y & 12y \\ y & 2 & -6y\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and first column:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}∗ & \frac{3}{2} & y \\ 25 & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & 2 & -6y\end{aligned}]
$$

The minor of ${m}_{21}$ is

 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2} & y \\ 2 & -6y\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2} & y \\ 2 & -6y\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\cdot (-6y)-y\cdot 2 \\  & =-11y.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of ${m}_{21}$ is $11$, so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}-11y & =11 \\ y & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y=-1.$
